results.title: Apple forums: 5.2.3 internet radio app using Radio Browser API
Apple forums: 5.2.3 'limit your app to streaming open-source stations only'
Apple forums: 5.2.3 internet radio player documentary evidence
The Infamous Apple Guideline 5.2.3 on Audio/Video Streaming

evidence.summary: Apple App Review repeatedly rejects aggregator radio apps (including ones built on Radio Browser) under Guideline 5.2.3 (unauthorized access to third-party audio streaming/discovery services); reviewers have asked to limit to stations with documented rights or provide documentary evidence, and evidence alone was sometimes not accepted. This is the main launch risk on iOS. Google Play side (foreground service type mediaPlayback declaration under Android 14+, background audio) not covered by this search: unverified. iOS needs UIBackgroundModes=audio, which is legitimate for an audio player.

evidence.query: TuneIn court ruling linking internet radio stations copyright Sony Warner; GDPR IP address third-party server LG Muenchen

results.title: Kluwer Copyright Blog: CJEU approach to communication to the public, internet radio
CMS: Court of Appeal sticks with CJEU jurisprudence: TuneIn v Warner
LG Muenchen I 3 O 17493/20 (Google Fonts IP transfer)
The Register: website fined over Google Fonts GDPR

evidence.summary: Copyright: Warner/Sony v TuneIn (UK High Court 2019, Court of Appeal 2021, applying CJEU 'communication to the public' case law) held that a radio directory app linking to stations not licensed for the listener's territory, and targeting those listeners, infringes; links to locally licensed stations did not. An EU-targeted aggregator faces the same doctrine. Privacy (GDPR): every stream play and Radio Browser query sends the device IP to a third-party server; LG Muenchen I (2022) treated an unconsented IP transfer to a third party as a GDPR violation (website case, EUR 100). Mitigation: privacy policy naming Radio Browser and station servers as recipients, no analytics without consent, no proxying of personal data; app-specific case law not found.

evidence.query: App Store privacy nutrition label data not collected app without analytics CCPA COPPA radio app requirements

results.title: conductatlas: Apple privacy nutrition labels requirement

evidence.summary: With favorites stored only on device and no account/analytics, the app can plausibly declare 'Data Not Collected' on Apple's label and a minimal Google Play Data safety form, but only if no analytics/crash SDK is added; labels are self-reported and frequently wrong. CCPA thresholds (revenue / volume of personal data) are unlikely to apply to a no-collection app, and COPPA applies only if directed to children under 13; neither checked against statute text here. US copyright for streams is the stations' responsibility (SoundExchange etc.), but aggregator liability was not researched for the US.

evidence.query: radio-browser.info api servers down outage mirrors de1 nl1 at1 availability

results.title: YCast issue #136: radio-browser server returns no entries

evidence.summary: Radio Browser is a volunteer-run, no-SLA service with a handful of mirrors; official guidance is to resolve all.api.radio-browser.info, randomize, and fail over (radio-browser-api does server discovery). Users have reported periods of unavailability. Ops plan: cache last directory results on device, retry next mirror on failure/429, keep favorites (with stream URL) usable offline from the directory, optionally self-host a mirror (AGPL server). No backend of our own is needed otherwise. Stream URLs go stale; use hideBroken and handle playback errors gracefully.

evidence.query: iOS App Transport Security NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia http audio stream Android cleartextTrafficPermitted radio app
evidence.summary: Many Icecast/Shoutcast streams are plain http. iOS ATS blocks them unless NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia (AVFoundation only; justification at review) or per-domain exceptions are set; Android 9+ blocks cleartext unless network_security_config permits it (Android side unverified by this search). Keep directory API and artwork on https, allow cleartext only for media. Other surfaces: untrusted strings from the directory/ICY metadata rendered as text only (no HTML/WebView), favicon URLs are arbitrary third-party hosts, RNTP 4.1.2 pulls kotlinaudio from JitPack and uses deprecated ExoPlayer2 (no security fixes), AsyncStorage 3.x ships a prebuilt SharedAsyncStorage.xcframework.

decision.rationale: Only fit-5 candidate under an MIT-compatible license: one native module covers HLS/MP3/AAC live playback (ExoPlayer2/AVPlayer), background service, lock-screen/notification controls and ICY metadata. Pin exactly 4.1.2: it is Apache-2.0 on npm and on the frozen v4 branch, while the repository default branch (main) and v5 (@rntp/player) are commercially licensed. Decision is extend, not adopt, because v4 is frozen (last release 2025-08-12, stale flag, total 68) and the app must be ready to carry patches (patch-package or a fork of the v4 branch) for RN New Architecture-only releases (0.82+) and Android SDK changes. Gate: spike on the target RN version before building UI.

alternatives.why_not: v5 rewrite is commercially licensed (npm license 'SEE LICENSE IN license.txt', paid for any for-profit/non-profit use, reported EUR 999/yr per app); license verdict unknown. Keep as paid fallback if v4 cannot run on the target RN.

MIT and well maintained (6.19.3) but fit 3: video component, notification controls tied to a mounted view, and Android onMetadata drops IcyInfo so ICY StreamTitle is lost (ev_e78da0233f0d). Best open-source fallback if RNTP v4 breaks.
MIT, maintained, fit 3: requires Expo modules runtime, lock-screen/now-playing and ICY metadata support weaker than RNTP.
Web Audio API engine, not a live-stream media player; fit 2.

component.name: background-media-controls
component.description: Keep audio playing in background; lock-screen, notification and remote (headset/CarPlay/Bluetooth) controls via Android MediaSession foreground service and iOS MPNowPlayingInfoCenter/MPRemoteCommandCenter.

decision.rationale: RNTP 4.1.2 already reads ICY in-band metadata from the same playback connection: Android MetadataAdapter maps ExoPlayer IcyInfo to key StreamTitle (keySpace icy) and emits Event.MetadataTimedReceived; iOS forwards AVPlayer timed metadata. Only a few lines of JS glue (split 'Artist - Title', empty-title handling) are needed. JS parsers would open a second stream connection per listener. v5 notes suggest Android ICY firing was improved later, so verify on device in the spike.

alternatives.why_not: Android onMetadata ignores IcyInfo (only Id3Frame/EventMessage), so StreamTitle needs a native patch.
Needs a parallel HTTP stream with Icy-MetaData:1, doubling bandwidth; stale.
LGPL-3.0-or-later (conditional) and also needs a parallel fetch stream; stale.

component.name: icy-metadata
component.description: Read ICY (Shoutcast/Icecast) in-band StreamTitle metadata (and HLS timed ID3) from live streams and surface it to JS for now-playing display.

decision.rationale: Radio Browser (free, no key, open community data, AGPL server self-hostable) is the intended directory and npm:radio-browser-api@6.0.3 (MIT, zero deps, ~5 KB) the intended client, but the vendor's own pages (radio-browser.info) were not reachable from this session, so pricing and data-use terms are only secondhand and the gate blocks adopt. alternatives.why_not: Preferred client, blocked only by unverified first-party service terms (service_terms_unverified); stale since 2025-05 but tiny and replaceable.
